work.name: Hispanic Society Museum & Library
work.summary: Administer the Hispanic Society's Archipelago digital repository and coordinate digitization and systems work across the Museum, Modern Library, and Prints and Photos departments.
highlights: Serve as primary administrator of Archipelago, an open-source Drupal/Solr digital repository: configuration, maintenance, troubleshooting, and front-end development (PHP, HTML, CSS) for the public Digital Collections site (diglib.hispanicsociety.org)

Build Python scripts (pandas, Pillow, ImageMagick) for bulk loading of metadata and images, including derivative generation (TIFF to JPG/PDF), cropping, CSV transformation, and reconciliation of metadata against linked-data sources
Write SQL queries and Python scripts to extract repository data into CSV reports for catalogers; compile system statistics and outcome reports for grant funders
Administer S3-compatible cloud object storage (Hetzner); working to automate transfers and backups with rclone
Coordinate systems work across the Museum, Modern Library, and Prints and Photos departments and their platforms (TMS, Archipelago), developing workflows tailored to each team and project
Designed the end-to-end digitization workflow, from project planning and imaging through upload and backup
Increased upload capacity by 500% by implementing batch uploading, uploaded 6,000+ objects, and launched the platform within 6 months of starting to meet grant deadlines

work.name: Hispanic American Periodicals Index
work.summary: Assist in cataloging journal articles for Latin American and Indigenous studies subjects for UCLA's HAPI search directory.
highlights:
Perform article-level cataloging for Latin American and Indigenous studies journals, applying LCSH
and FAST-based controlled vocabularies to ensure accurate subject access

Create detailed and descriptive metadata by analyzing article content, identifying key themes,
authors, and focus, and applying accurate terms that correct bias in legacy subject headings

work.name: Division of Libraries, New York University
work.summary: Supported the department's DH grant opportunities, and supported faculty and student projects with consultation, workshops, advice, and guidance
highlights: Developed research guides, tutorials, and LibGuides to assist in navigating digital humanities, IIIF standards, and creating digital collections
Provided reference and research consultations to faculty and graduate students across disciplines, with a focus on sustainable web development and web archiving practices
Taught workshops on static websites, introductory programming, and digital preservation using CollectionBuilder, Wax, Jekyll, and GitHub Pages
Supported the Digital Humanities grant program for faculty and students, reporting on grant results, crafting blog posts, and supporting projects through platform consultation

work.name: Division of Libraries, New York University
work.summary: Created workflows and resources for using IIIF standards, IIIF-compatible content, and creating new IIIF materials by surveying potential users and implementers.
highlights:
Created step-by-step GitHub-based tutorials for implementing IIIF, enabling library staff and
researchers to use image APIs, manifests, and viewers without advanced programming skills

Led the conference presentation, “DIY IIIF: A Sample of Standalone, Static, and Skunkworks
Implementations” at the 2024 IIIF Annual Conference, introducing scalable IIIF adoption and emphasizing sustainable, low-barrier implementation

Served as a point of contact for IIIF at NYU, fostering shared understanding of IIIF capabilities
across archives, IT, and subject liaisons to promote strategic alignment with departmental priorities

work.name: Center for Latin American and Caribbean Studies, New York University
work.summary: Led the first major effort to catalog the CLACS Quechua Library, resulting in the creation of Runakunaq Bibliotecanku (see Projects). Assisted with departmental events through promotion and administrative support.
highlights: Established collection policies and organization systems for the CLACS Classroom Library
Increased accessibility of social media posts by providing image descriptions for posts
Designed and maintained the Chile 1973/2023 website to highlight programming and resources
Supported departmental events by creating flyers, organizing speakers, and assisting with events

work.name: Epicenter NYC
work.summary: Contributed to the weekly newsletter with Quechua language learnings. Reported for citywide COVID-19 and MPV grant programs, including social media outreach, community programming, and vaccination efforts. Also managed the schedule for CEO/Founder Mitra Kalita.

projects.name: Digitizing Cronicawan
projects.summary: An online, static digital archive featuring Cronicawan, a newspaper published during the 1970s revolution in Cusco. A collaboration with the Centro Bartolomé de las Casas in Cusco, Peru, and my Master's thesis project.
highlights: Open Access, Andean Studies, Quechua

Led the digitization, cataloguing, metadata creation, and access design for a bilingual digital archive
featuring Cronicawan

Developed a structured archival database for preservation and discovery using DACS- and EAD-
based standards, presented through a static site built with Wax and Jekyll
Developed a custom Transkribus model that recognizes print media formats and Quechua language, keeping data local to the project

Assessed cultural, linguistic, and ethical considerations in preserving Indigenous media, designing for
community and scholarly use while maintaining data integrity and respecting original contexts

projects.name: Runakunaq Bibliotecanku
projects.summary: An open-access library and catalog for NYU's Center for Latin American Studies' holdings on Andean studies, Quechua language, and worldwide Indigenous studies.
highlights: Open Access, Andean Studies, Quechua

Developed metadata description, preservation, and discovery workflows for the collection, enhancing
accessibility and long-term stewardship

Collaborated with community members, students, and faculty to ensure culturally respectful
representation, appropriate access, and alignment with CARE and FAIR principles

projects.name: EcStatic Magic: Static Sites for DH Projects
projects.summary: A hands-on workshop introducing static site generation tools to faculty and students interested in DH projects.
highlights: Developed and delivered a workshop introducing static site generation tools, including CollectionBuilder, Jekyll, and GitHub Pages
Focused on empowering faculty and students to independently design and maintain digital archives, fostering knowledge sharing and digital preservation
